answer: Sybil resistance comes from issuing each agent identity only after remote attestation verifies its enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE), then binding the identity to a non-exportable enclave key. A copied VM cannot reproduce that hardware-backed proof or key, so scaling identities requires additional enclave-capable silicon rather than virtual clones. MRENCLAVE alone does not ensure one identity per chip; issuance policy must enforce uniqueness. Like summit, timber, and harbor infrastructure, the barrier depends on real resources.
